review_notes: Read the whole target file. It declares no simp lemmas or attributes; the only simp-interface issue found concerns the `Series.map` API in the imported definitions file. I read `Series` and `Series.map` in Def_CerednikDrinfeld_SpecialFormalModule.lean and grepped for an apply/constantCoeff lemma, finding none. I did not check whether the tail of `solution` or the `Thm_*` imports contain such a lemma. This is a modest finding, since the fix belongs in the definitions file rather than the target.

findings.excerpt: let φp : Series Rp := fun i => MvPowerSeries.map (algebraMap R Rp) (φ i)
findings.problem: `Series.map` is already the canonical base change of a `Series`, but it has no `Series.map_apply` lemma (rfl) and no simp lemma for `constantCoeff ((φ.map f) i)`. The proof therefore re-defines `φp` by hand as a lambda instead of `φ.map (algebraMap R Rp)`. It then needs a manual `change` to unfold the lambda before `MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff_map` can fire. The same `show … MvPowerSeries.map f (φ i)` unfolding appears in the definitions file (for example in `IsLawHom.map` and `Series.map_comp`). So the simp normal form of `(Series.map f φ) i` is not exposed, and each user must unfold the definition by hand.
findings.proposed_change: In Def_CerednikDrinfeld_SpecialFormalModule.lean, add `@[simp] theorem Series.map_apply (f : B →+* B') (φ : Series B) (i : Fin 2) : (φ.map f) i = MvPowerSeries.map f (φ i) := rfl`. Optionally add a `constantCoeff_map` variant for `Series`. Then use `let φp := φ.map (algebraMap R Rp)` here, so that `hφp0` becomes `by simp [hφ0]` or `rw [Series.map_apply, MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff_map, hφ0, map_zero]`, with no `change`. The orientation is safe because it unfolds a non-recursive definition into the standard Mathlib `MvPowerSeries.map`.
findings.benefit: The unfolding step disappears from the proof. `φp` becomes the library's standard `Series.map`, so the existing lemmas `Series.map_comp`, `Series.map_map` and `Series.map_id` apply to it. Any later use of `(φ.map f) i` also normalises to Mathlib's `MvPowerSeries.map` and its simp lemmas.

evidence.excerpt: def Series.map (f : B →+* B') (φ : Series B) : Series B' := fun i => MvPowerSeries.map f (φ i)
